title: How do we find the lowest common multiple of four groups?
description: Four groups of numbers are each written as products of primes. Each prime is kept the biggest number of times it appears in any number of the group, and multiplying gives that group's lowest common multiple. Each answer is then checked by dividing it by the numbers it came from.
teaching_notes: One idea: keep every prime found in any number of the group, each the biggest number of times, then multiply. Ask the class which primes the third group needs before the working is shown. Watch for students who drop a prime that is found in only one number.

video_script.why: The child has built the lowest common multiple of two numbers from the biggest count of each prime and now meets four groups, one of them with three numbers.
video_script.substitution: For each group write the prime products, keep every prime the biggest number of times it appears, and multiply.
video_script.anchor: Four groups of numbers in a column: 30 and 72; 36 and 54; 105, 195 and 65; 222 and 370.
video_script.payoff_line: The lowest common multiples are three hundred sixty and one hundred eight

final_answer.spoken: three hundred sixty, one hundred eight, one thousand three hundred sixty five and one thousand one hundred ten

never_show: a group answer before its own step
maths_rules: 30 = 2 × 3 × 5 and 72 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3; biggest counts: 2 three times, 3 twice, 5 once; LCM = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 360
36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 and 54 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3; biggest counts: 2 twice, 3 three times; LCM = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 108
video_script.design: One idea: keep every prime found in any number of the group, each the biggest number of times. The four groups stay in the anchor band all video and each step lights one group. The check divides each answer by the numbers it came from.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>We must find the lowest common multiple of four groups. The lowest number that all numbers of a group divide is called their lowest common multiple.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>First, thirty and seventy two. Second, thirty six and fifty four.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Third, one hundred five, one hundred ninety five and sixty five. Fourth, two hundred twenty two and three hundred seventy.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>How do we find each one?

beats.on_screen: the four groups stay still; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: piles of prime cards: the biggest pile of each prime is lit; a prime found in only one number still has its pile kept

marks.m1: piles of prime cards appear for two numbers, the biggest pile of each prime is lit
marks.m2: a prime found in only one of the numbers has its pile kept

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We keep each prime the biggest number of times it appears in any number of the group.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A prime found in only one number is kept too.

marks.m1: the given line is written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, four groups of numbers.

beats.on_screen: To find: the LCM of each group

marks.m1: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the lowest common multiple of each group.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, first group: 30 = 2 × 3 × 5; 72 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3; keep 2 three times, 3 twice, 5 once; LCM = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 360

marks.m2: three 2s, two 3s and one 5 are lit and LCM = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 360 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, the first group. Thirty is two times three times five. Seventy two is three twos times two threes.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Keep three twos, two threes and a five, which multiply to three hundred sixty.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, second group: 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3; 54 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3; keep 2 twice and 3 three times; LCM = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 108

marks.m2: two 2s and three 3s are lit and LCM = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 108 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, the second group. Thirty six has two twos and two threes. Fifty four has one two and three threes.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Keep two twos and three threes, which multiply to one hundred eight.

marks.m3: 3, 5, 7 and 13 are lit and LCM = 3 × 5 × 7 × 13 = 1365 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, the third group has three numbers. One hundred five is three times five times seven. One hundred ninety five is three times five times thirteen.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Sixty five is five times thirteen.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Keep three, five, seven and thirteen once each, which multiply to one thousand three hundred sixty five.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, fourth group: 222 = 2 × 3 × 37; 370 = 2 × 5 × 37; keep 2, 3, 5 and 37 once each; LCM = 2 × 3 × 5 × 37 = 1110

marks.m2: 2, 3, 5 and 37 are lit and LCM = 2 × 3 × 5 × 37 = 1110 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, the fourth group. Two hundred twenty two is two times three times thirty seven. Three hundred seventy is two times five times thirty seven.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Keep two, three, five and thirty seven once each, which multiply to one thousand one hundred ten.

marks.m1: the word check is written above the divisions
marks.m2: the divisions for the first and second groups are written, all whole numbers
marks.m3: the divisions for the third and fourth groups are written, all whole numbers

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step five, check that each answer divides exactly by every number in its group.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Three hundred sixty divides by thirty and seventy two. One hundred eight divides by thirty six and fifty four.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The third answer divides by all three of its numbers, and the fourth by both of its numbers.

marks.m1: the first two answers are written and boxed
marks.m2: the last two answers are written and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The lowest common multiples are three hundred sixty and one hundred eight.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The other two are one thousand three hundred sixty five and one thousand one hundred ten.
